candidates.name: SQLite Health Check
candidates.problem: Use before accepting a local database backup or when diagnosing application data inconsistencies.
candidates.author: SQLite authors
candidates.inputs: A stable, offline SQLite snapshot without adjacent WAL/SHM/journal files; zero-byte files are valid empty databases.
candidates.outputs: JSON healthy flag, structural check results and up to 1000 foreign-key violations.
candidates.existing_tests: New independent implementation: tests/test_verified_batch.py; no upstream tests reused.
limitations: Checks trusted local databases; not a hardened parser for hostile SQLite files.
The SQLite VM progress callback and lock timeout cannot forcibly interrupt stalled operating-system I/O.
Rejects adjacent WAL/SHM/journal files; use the SQLite backup API to create a consistent offline snapshot first.
Foreign-key findings are capped at 1000; truncated=true means more exist.
security_considerations: Immutable read-only connection; no locks, journal writes, repairs, supplied SQL or extension loading. Requires a stable trusted offline snapshot. Never remove active journals to bypass checks.
candidates.license_review: Original implementation under repository MIT license. Reference APIs/formats only; no upstream source or prose copied. Unknown documentation licenses are not permission to copy. Source revision/maintenance timestamps are null when not verified.
candidates.security_review: Reviewed local implementation and standard-library dependencies. No downloaded code executed; no external endpoints, third-party installs, shell execution, privilege escalation or production credentials. Bounded inputs/output as documented.
candidates.decision: Accepted after offline behavioral tests on macOS; not published or released.

candidates.name: ZIP Safety Audit
candidates.problem: Inspect downloaded archives before choosing a trusted extraction tool.
candidates.author: Python Software Foundation
candidates.source_revision: Python zipfile documentation (rolling; no code copied)
candidates.inputs: One ZIP archive no larger than 64 MiB; contents are never decompressed.
candidates.outputs: JSON member count, declared size and indexed hazard findings.
candidates.existing_tests: New independent implementation: tests/test_verified_batch.py; no upstream tests reused.
limitations: Metadata-only heuristic: does not verify CRCs, actual compressed streams, malware, recursive archives, or every filesystem collision.
Case-insensitive duplicate detection can flag harmless names on case-sensitive filesystems.
Memory is proportional to the ZIP central directory, bounded indirectly by the 64 MiB input limit.
security_considerations: Never extracts or decompresses entries. Flags absolute and parent paths, Windows path hazards, special files, symlinks, encrypted members and suspicious metadata. A report without findings is not an assurance that extraction is safe.

candidates.name: JSON Lines Key Profile
candidates.problem: Detect schema drift and malformed records in event streams or dataset exports before ingestion.
candidates.author: Python Software Foundation
candidates.inputs: UTF-8 JSON Lines; one object per nonblank physical line. A final newline is optional.
candidates.outputs: JSON record counts, invalid line numbers, and top-level key coverage.
candidates.existing_tests: New independent implementation: tests/test_verified_batch.py; no upstream tests reused.
limitations: Counts top-level keys only; null values count as present.
Rejects duplicate object keys at any depth, non-object records, malformed UTF-8, NaN and Infinity constants.
At most 10000 distinct keys and 1000 invalid line numbers are retained. Blank lines are counted separately.
security_considerations: Streams with a bounded line buffer. Reports key names and line numbers, never values. Key names may themselves be sensitive. Reaching a resource limit emits no partial success report.

candidates.name: CSV Key Reconciliation
candidates.problem: Reconcile customer exports, migration results or inventory snapshots using one identifier column.
candidates.author: Ruby contributors
candidates.source_revision: Ruby 2.6 API documentation; no code copied
dependencies: Ruby >=2.6 with csv, json, optparse and set standard libraries
candidates.inputs: Two comma-delimited UTF-8 CSV files with unique nonempty headers, consistent row widths and a common named key column. UTF-8 BOM and quoted multiline fields are supported.
candidates.outputs: JSON row counts, common-key count, keys unique to each file and duplicate keys.
candidates.existing_tests: New independent implementation: tests/test_verified_batch.py; no upstream tests reused.
limitations: Exact string comparison preserves case and surrounding whitespace; no numeric normalization or value comparison.
Files are limited to 32 MiB each; memory grows with unique key count.
Header-only CSVs are valid empty datasets; zero-byte files are invalid.
security_considerations: Reads both files and writes only to stdout. Output contains key values, which can be personal or confidential; handle the report accordingly. Does not merge or alter exports.

candidates.name: npm Lockfile Policy Audit
candidates.problem: Review supply-chain metadata before permitting a dependency installation in CI.
candidates.author: npm contributors
candidates.source_revision: npm CLI v11 documentation; no code or prose copied
candidates.inputs: npm package-lock.json lockfileVersion 2 or 3 with a packages object, at most 32 MiB and 100000 entries.
candidates.outputs: JSON checked/skipped counts and per-package policy findings.
candidates.existing_tests: New independent implementation: tests/test_verified_batch.py; no upstream tests reused.
limitations: Metadata policy only: does not verify downloaded content, package safety, advisories or manifest consistency.

candidates.name: HAR Timing Summary
candidates.problem: Inspect browser network captures for slow requests or failing responses before sharing aggregate diagnostics.
candidates.author: HAR specification authors / Web Performance Working Group
candidates.source_revision: HAR 1.2 specification; no code or prose copied
candidates.inputs: HAR 1.2 JSON with log.entries; entries need finite nonnegative time, response status/bodySize and a timings object. At most 32 MiB and 100000 entries.
candidates.outputs: JSON aggregate timing, status, slow-request and known body-size statistics.
candidates.existing_tests: New independent implementation: tests/test_verified_batch.py; no upstream tests reused.
limitations: An aggregate reader, not full HAR schema validation; optional/missing timing components are ignored.
Summed durations include overlapping requests and are not page-load wall time; SSL timing overlaps connect timing.
Failure counts use status 0 or >=400; redirects are not classified as failures. Unknown body sizes (-1) are counted separately.
security_considerations: Reads locally without network access. Report and errors omit URLs, headers, cookies, query parameters and response bodies. Original HAR files often contain secrets; this tool does not redact the original file.

candidates.name: PEM Certificate Expiry Report
candidates.problem: Use before deploying certificate bundles or to monitor offline certificate inventories.
candidates.author: The Go Authors
candidates.inputs: One regular PEM file up to 8 MiB containing at most 512 X.509 CERTIFICATE blocks. Whitespace between blocks is allowed; private keys, other block types, nested markers and leading/trailing text are rejected.
candidates.outputs: JSON observation time, certificate SHA-256 fingerprints, validity dates, remaining seconds and statuses.
candidates.existing_tests: Independent native Go tests with generated/local fixtures; Python integration tests exercise CLI and exit codes.
limitations: Date inspection does not verify certificate trust, signatures, DNS names, key usage or revocation.
Expiry begins at the exact not_after instant. Dates at or before the warning-window boundary are expiring.
Reports fingerprints and dates rather than subject names, SANs, certificate bytes or private material.
security_considerations: Reads local certificate data only. It does not contact issuers, load private keys, modify trust stores or renew certificates. Process a stable local file; filesystem I/O deadlines are controlled by the operating system.
candidates.license_review: API reference only. New MIT implementation; no upstream code or prose copied. Go reference license BSD-3-Clause verified at go.dev/LICENSE.
candidates.security_review: Design reviewed: local reads, no networking, subprocesses, extension loading or credential access.
candidates.decision: Accepted after native Go/vet/race checks and CLI integration on macOS. Not published; cross-platform CI results tracked separately.

candidates.name: CIDR Overlap Report
candidates.problem: Check address plans, VPN allocations or firewall inventories before provisioning overlapping subnets.
candidates.author: The Go Authors
candidates.inputs: A UTF-8 text file up to 2 MiB with one IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR per line. Blank lines and whole-line # comments are ignored. Up to 4096 network records and 64 KiB per line are accepted; inline comments and zone identifiers are invalid.
candidates.outputs: JSON normalized networks, overlap count, overlapping line-number pairs and truncation status.
candidates.existing_tests: Independent native Go tests with generated/local fixtures; Python integration tests exercise CLI and exit codes.
limitations: IPv4 and IPv6 are separate address families; IPv4-mapped IPv6 prefixes remain IPv6.
Host bits are masked before comparison, so differently written allocations can become duplicates.
All pairs are compared; the 4096-record limit bounds the quadratic work. Output pairs retain input order.
Empty/comment-only input is a valid empty allocation list.
security_considerations: Reads only the supplied file. It sends no packets, resolves no names and changes no routes or firewall rules. Reports include network allocations, which may be sensitive.
candidates.license_review: API reference only. New MIT implementation; no upstream code or prose copied. Go reference license BSD-3-Clause verified at go.dev/LICENSE.
candidates.security_review: Design reviewed: local reads, no networking, subprocesses, extension loading or credential access.
candidates.decision: Accepted after native Go/vet/race checks and CLI integration on macOS. Not published; cross-platform CI results tracked separately.

candidates.name: SHA-256 Manifest Verification
candidates.problem: Check backups, transferred assets and archived media against a previously trusted manifest. Accepts the array format produced by image-checksum-manifest.
candidates.author: The Go Authors
candidates.inputs: An 8 MiB maximum JSON array of at most 10000 unique objects, each with exactly path (relative forward-slash path), bytes (nonnegative integer), and sha256 (64 hexadecimal digits). Duplicate or unknown fields, duplicate paths, absolute paths, dot/parent traversal, backslashes and colon-qualified paths are rejected.
candidates.outputs: JSON verified count and per-path missing, unsafe, unreadable or changed findings.
candidates.existing_tests: Independent native Go tests with generated/local fixtures; Python integration tests exercise CLI and exit codes.
limitations: Requires Go 1.24 or newer for the traversal-resistant os.Root API. Use a currently maintained Go release.
Relative symlinks resolving inside the selected root are allowed; symlinks escaping the root are refused. Absolute symlinks may be refused even if they point into the root.
Use a stable directory tree. This does not defend against hostile mount changes, hard links, or special-file replacement races by another local process.
Files absent from the manifest are ignored. Empty arrays are valid. This checks integrity relative to a trusted manifest, not authenticity or malware.
A total hashing-budget failure returns exit 2 without a partial success report. Hashes are streamed rather than loading file contents into memory.
security_considerations: Opens files for reading through os.OpenRoot. The selected root itself may be a symlink and must be trusted. Files, manifests and backups are not modified or removed. Missing/nonregular/unsafe files produce findings; other read failures abort without reporting success.
candidates.license_review: API reference only. New MIT implementation; no upstream code or prose copied. Go reference license BSD-3-Clause verified at go.dev/LICENSE.
candidates.security_review: Design reviewed: local reads, no networking, subprocesses, extension loading or credential access.
candidates.decision: Accepted after native Go/vet/race checks and CLI integration on macOS. Not published; cross-platform CI results tracked separately.
